instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Make Help Define Us
cards.instruction: Get their help, then use how it is offered to redefine what the relationship means.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take the far end of my table. Today I'm promoting you from rescuer to partner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm stronger. I can carry it on my own.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No, you'll leave this end to me. A partner trusts me with something heavy.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All right. Where do you want us to put it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the question I wanted. Stay there while I clear the corner; then we'll choose the angle together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Check the spelling in my complaint. Leave the angry sentence exactly where I've put it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a good sentence. I only wanted to fix one word.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you're my collaborator, not my minder. Fix the word and put your name beside mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I like the sentence, but I don't want my name on the complaint.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then keep yours off. We'll call you my editor, and I'll take the blame. You can tell people you tried to restrain me.

cards.title: Reopen the First Reason
cards.instruction: Keep them present by returning to the first reason for staying and revealing that it now means something different.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Stay until the tea cools. You always rush goodbye.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's cold now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then I wasn't really waiting for the tea.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What were you waiting for?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A goodbye that doesn't sound like you're already somewhere else. Have another sip.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave the key on my table, then sit down. Returning it isn't a doorstep job.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's on the table. I only came to give it back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then give me ten minutes as well. I want to see whether you can still visit when you have to knock.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Would you actually let me in next time?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. But next time you ask that at the door. Today you're already in, so choose a chair and tell me when you're coming back.

cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Change What the Apology Is For
cards.instruction: Get an apology, then reveal that the original offense was only the first layer of what needs repair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Thank you for apologising for missing my concert.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: So we're okay?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Closer. Now why did I have to ask whether you'd noticed missing it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I didn't know what to say.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then apologise for letting me rehearse your apology alone all week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I accept your apology for breaking my vase. Now tell me when you knew the dog hadn't done it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Straight away. I'll buy you another vase.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep your money. You watched me shut the dog out of this room for three days. That is the part you're going to put right.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was embarrassed to admit it. Shall I let him back in?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Call him in. Then apologise to me for leaving me to punish him. Your embarrassment stopped you speaking; mine began when I found out who I'd believed.

cards.title: Approve the Harmless Version
cards.instruction: Get approval for a harmless version of your plan, then gradually reveal what that approval now commits them to.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One extra chair in the hall won't trouble you, will it? Put it at the head of the table for me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's fine. I'll move it over.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I'll sit there for the tenants' meeting tonight. Leave the other chairs around it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I agreed to move a chair, not host your meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then sit beside me and explain that distinction when we begin. I'll put use of the hall first, since you've raised it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Aunt May and Uncle Rob can come for tea, can't they? I'll have them here at four.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Of course. I'll put the kettle on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Their cousins are driving them, so set a few more places. We'll make everyone welcome.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How many places? I only have six cups.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Six will do for the first sitting. Keep the kettle on and I'll bring the others through once we've cleared. You offered tea; I'll handle the seating.

cards.title: The Handoff Already Happened
cards.instruction: Get them to accept responsibility by returning to earlier offers until the task seems to have been assigned all along.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said you'd take over the wedding arrivals. Start by phoning the guests who haven't replied to our invitations.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant I'd answer the door on the day.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. You need to know who's coming to it. Use this list and mark their answers beside their names.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I offered to let people in, not chase them beforehand.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then make these the calls that let them in without confusion. I have your name against arrivals already; tell me when you've finished the list.
